correctness.rationale: For fixed positive \(\sigma\), the source factorized Jacobian reduces conjugate times to roots of \(F=A\sigma^2+B\). At \((\tau,\alpha)=(\pi,0)\), \(F=0\), \(F_\tau=-\pi^3(1+4\sigma^2)/2\), \(F_\alpha=0\), and \(F_{\alpha\alpha}=2\pi^4\sigma^2\). The implicit-function theorem gives \(\tau^{\prime\prime}(0)=4\pi\sigma^2/(1+4\sigma^2)\), so the phase coefficient is \(\kappa(\sigma)=2\pi\sigma^2/(1+4\sigma^2)\). The same calculation applies at \(\alpha=\pi\); the source no-conjugate-points-before-cut result identifies the nearby branch as the first conjugate time.

value.rationale: The cut time measures when a geodesic ceases to minimize globally; the conjugate time measures the first singularity of the exponential map. The exact profile \(\kappa(\sigma)=2\pi\sigma^2/(1+4\sigma^2)\) quantifies how the conjugate-time branch leaves the two exceptional phases for every fixed positive pitch. Its strict increase and finite limit \(\pi/2\) provide a natural local sensitivity scale for optimal-synthesis analysis and conditioning, beyond a qualitative equality criterion.
